title: A Systematic Survey on Unified Compression-Encryption Schemes with a Header-Consolidation Taxonomy
content: Data compression and encryption are conventionally performed as sequential operations, incurring redundant computational overhead, increasing the attack surface, and complicating system architectures. This systematic literature review analyzes 34 verified contributions published between 1948 and 2026 in IEEE, ACM, Springer, Elsevier, Wiley, IET, and NIST venues, following PRISMA 2020. We propose a four-level operational taxonomy (L0–L3) for defining what it means for a scheme to be unified rather than merely coordinated as well as the structure of header consolidation: an L3 scheme consolidates the compression and encryption headers into a single object, typically carried by the key. Only two schemes achieve L3, both restricted by domain-specific assumptions. We discover two structural constraints—the redundancy duality and the header duality—which explain why L3 schemes are restricted to domain-specific, and that the latter is a security constraint: the compression header leaks source statistics and the encryption header leaks cryptographic state, so consolidating them reduces the attack surface. We also show that source-type specificity is inherited by all joint schemes reviewed, and the review also reveals that no scheme achieves a source-independent compression ratio, and that formal security proofs under standard adversarial models (IND-CPA, IND-CCA, IND-CCA2, AE) are absent in each of the reviewed schemes, including the two L3 schemes.
